title: Glasslands - an HTML RPG prototype in the style of classic BBS door games.
author: BrandeX

comments.author: BrandeX
comments.body:
I've been experimenting with AI-assisted game development and wanted to share a project I've been working on called **GLASSLANDS: Lamplighters of the Long Noon**.

It's a single-player, post-apocalyptic RPG inspired by old BBS door games, classic Wasteland, Fallout, and roguelikes.

The premise is that an orbital mirror network designed to cool the planet went rogue and scorched the surface into glass. You play as a Lamplighter, a scout tasked with maintaining a network of beacons that protect settlements from the deadly sunlight.

The game demo features:

- A 99×99 tile overworld with multiple regions to explore
- Turn-based combat, equipment, leveling, and loot
- Survival mechanics including heat, food, and water
- Towns, shops, banking, quests, and dungeons
- Factions, reputation, and multiple story endings
- An emoji-based graphical style

**The development process has been almost entirely AI-assisted.** I started with a detailed game design document of over 2,600 lines and used AI to help turn it into a playable HTML/JavaScript prototype.

The game runs directly in a browser, with no installation required. I'm aiming for an old-school RPG experience with modern accessibility, while keeping the presentation simple and lightweight.

One interesting challenge has been getting AI to produce something that doesn't just technically function, but actually feels like a proper game. The interface, visual consistency, game balance, and gameplay interactions have required quite a bit of iteration.

It's still very much a work in progress, and I'm experimenting with what works and what doesn't.

I'd be interested to hear what other AI game developers think, especially about the emoji-based presentation and whether this kind of old-school RPG is something you'd enjoy playing.
